{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''William Buhmann Johnson''' (born December 5, 1944) is an American mathematician, one of the namesakes of the [[Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma]]. He is Distinguished Professor and A.G. & M.E. Owen Chair of Mathematics at [[Texas A&M University]]. His research specialties include the theory of [[Banach space]]s, [[nonlinear functional analysis]], and [[probability theory]].<ref>[http://www.math.tamu.edu/directory/formalpg.php?user=johnson Faculty directory listing], Texas A&M Mathematics, retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref> He was born in [[Palo Alto, California]] and raised from an early age in [[Dallas, Texas]].

Johnson graduated from [[Southern Methodist University]] in 1966,<ref>[http://www.math.tamu.edu/~johnson/ Faculty web page], retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref>  and earned a doctorate from [[Iowa State University]] in 1969 under the supervision of James A. Dyer.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=William Buhmann Johnson|id=118}}</ref> After faculty positions at the [[University of Houston]], and [[Ohio State University]], he joined the Texas A&M faculty in 1984.

In 2007, Johnson was awarded the [[Stefan Banach Medal]] of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[https://www.impan.pl/en/events/awards/stefan-banach-medal Stefan Banach Medal] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201105125729/https://www.impan.pl/en/events/awards/stefan-banach-medal |date=2020-11-05 }}, [[Polish Academy of Sciences]], retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref><ref>[http://www.math.tamu.edu/news/2007pers.html 2007 Personal News], Texas A&M Mathematics, retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref> In 2018 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{cite book|author=Johnson, William B.|chapter=Some 20+ year old problems about Banach spaces and operators on them|title=Proceedings of the ICM – 2018 Rio de Janeiro|volume=2|pages=1669–1686|chapter-url=http://www.math.tamu.edu/~bill.johnson/mainREVISED.pdf|archive-date=2018-08-26|access-date=2018-08-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826005236/http://www.math.tamu.edu/~bill.johnson/mainREVISED.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> His doctoral students include [[Edward Odell]].
